learning.title: Graft hook generators plus git stash in a worktree produce an alarming unmerged-index state
learning.trigger: A seat's git index goes unmerged mid-session with no merge in progress; git stash trips over tracked-looking generated paths (.cursor/hooks.json, .github/copilot-instructions.md) and stash pop refuses.
learning.rule: Graft hook generators write files that appear tracked in worktrees; a git stash then captures an index state the pop cannot restore, and the index reports unmerged with no merge running. The recovery that worked (2026-11-16, dev-bugfix on PR #501): restore the two tracked .claude/helpers files to HEAD, clear only the untracked generated paths, and verify the branch diff is exactly the intended change before continuing. Do not run git stash in a worktree where graft hooks have run until the generated paths are explicitly excluded; prefer committing or stashing with pathspecs. The state looks alarming but is recoverable - check the branch diff against the intended change before assuming corruption.

verification.requirement: Prove the recovery by diff: after restoring tracked files to HEAD and clearing the generated untracked paths, git status must be clean and the branch diff must equal exactly the intended change (the 4-line mkdir fix verified this way). Record which generated paths the hook writes in the seat handover so a successor recognizes them instantly.
